title: Understanding a Contract
text:
A contract is a legally binding agreement between two or more parties. Each party agrees to perform specific obligations, and the terms of the agreement must be clear enough for everyone to understand. If one party fails to meet its obligations, the other party may be entitled to seek compensation. For this reason, careful reading before signing is essential.

Many contracts also include a clause that explains how disputes will be resolved. Some agreements require mediation before the parties go to court, because this process is usually faster and less expensive. In addition, a well-written contract often states how the agreement may be ended. Therefore, people who sign a contract should understand both their rights and their responsibilities.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what must the terms of an agreement be?
options: clear enough for everyone to understand

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, why do some agreements require mediation?
options: because the process is usually faster and less expensive
because courts no longer accept contracts
because mediation is required by law for all contracts
because the parties never sign agreements

questions.text: What can be inferred about a party that fails to meet its obligations?
options: It may have to pay compensation.
It is automatically excused from the contract.
It can always avoid going to court.
It must rewrite the contract for free.

questions.text: Why does the author recommend careful reading before signing a contract?
options: Because a contract can affect people's rights and responsibilities.
Because contracts are always written to favour one side.
Because signing a contract is only a formality.

vocabulary.definition: a legally binding agreement between two or more parties
duties that a person or party is legally required to perform
money or something else given to make up for a loss or harm
a process in which a neutral person helps two sides reach an agreement

paragraph_translations: Um contrato é um acordo juridicamente vinculativo entre duas ou mais partes. Cada parte concorda em cumprir obrigações específicas, e os termos do acordo devem ser claros o suficiente para que todos compreendam. Se uma parte não cumprir suas obrigações, a outra pode ter direito a buscar compensação. Por isso, ler com atenção antes de assinar é essencial.

Muitos contratos também incluem uma cláusula que explica como as disputas serão resolvidas. Alguns acordos exigem mediação antes que as partes recorram aos tribunais, porque esse processo costuma ser mais rápido e menos caro. Além disso, um contrato bem redigido geralmente indica como o acordo pode ser encerrado. Portanto, quem assina um contrato deve compreender tanto seus direitos quanto suas responsabilidades.
